title: South African Republic
capsule: The Zuid-Afrikaansche Republiek (South African Republic), commonly called the Transvaal, was a Boer republic established north of the Vaal River when Britain recognised Afrikaner independence via the Sand River Convention of 17 January 1852. Britain annexed the state in 1877 but was forced to restore its independence after the Boers defeated British forces in the First Boer War (1880–1881), and the London Convention of 1884 granted full sovereignty under Paul Kruger, who served as State President from 1883. The discovery of the Witwatersrand gold reefs in 1886 drew massive foreign immigration and ultimately British imperial aggression; the Second Boer War (1899–1902) ended with the Treaty of Vereeniging on 31 May 1902 converting the republic into the British Transvaal Colony.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial extent is well attested through British and Boer administrative records and surveyed boundaries, though the western frontier with the Bechuanaland Protectorate was intermittently disputed.
